tools.name: CancelMeeting
tools.description:
Cancels a Microsoft Teams meeting the signed-in user organizes, notifying attendees.

Only the meeting's organizer can cancel it; cancelling a meeting organized by someone else
fails.

parameters.name: meeting_id
parameters.description: The ID of the meeting to cancel.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: An optional message included in the cancellation notice sent to attendees. Defaults to empty (no comment).

output.description: Confirmation that the meeting was cancelled.

comment.value: Due to a scheduling conflict, this meeting has been cancelled. We will reschedule shortly. Apologies for any inconvenience.

tools.name: CreateChat
tools.description:
Creates a Microsoft Teams chat.

For a 1:1 chat (exactly one other member besides the caller), the MS Graph API deduplicates
reliably: if a one-on-one chat already exists with that member, this returns the existing
chat instead of creating a new one.

For a group chat (two or more other members), the MS Graph API does NOT guarantee dedup: a
new group chat may be created even when a group chat with the exact same member set already
exists. To reuse an existing group chat, look it up first (e.g. via `Teams.GetChatMetadata`
or `Teams.ListChats`) rather than relying on this tool to return it.

Provide any combination of user_ids and/or user_names. When available, prefer providing
user_ids for optimal performance.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The IDs of the users to create a chat with.

parameters.name: user_names
parameters.description: The names of the users to create a chat with.

tools.name: CreateMeeting
tools.description:
Schedules a new Microsoft Teams online meeting on the signed-in user's calendar.

Creates a calendar event with an attached Teams meeting (join link, dial-in info) and sends
invites to any attendees provided. The response's join_url is what attendees use to join.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The meeting's subject/title.

parameters.name: start_datetime
parameters.description: The meeting's start date and time, interpreted in time_zone. Provide a string in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'.

parameters.name: end_datetime
parameters.description: The meeting's end date and time, interpreted in time_zone. Provide a string in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'.

parameters.name: time_zone
parameters.description: The IANA (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles') or Windows (e.g. 'Pacific Standard Time') time zone that start_datetime and end_datetime are expressed in. Defaults to 'UTC'.

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: Email addresses of people to invite to the meeting. Optional.

parameters.name: attendee_names
parameters.description: Names of people to invite to the meeting; each is resolved to a unique email address. Prefer attendee_emails when the email address is already known, since name resolution adds latency and fails when a name is ambiguous or not found. Optional.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Plain-text meeting description/agenda shown in the invite body. Defaults to empty (no description).

output.description: The Teams meeting that was scheduled.

description.value: Quarterly review of the product roadmap. Please come prepared with updates on your team's milestones and any blockers for Q4 planning.

tools.name: GetChannelMessages
tools.description:
Retrieves the messages in a Microsoft Teams channel, newest first.

The channel-messages endpoint rejects server-side date filtering outright, so start_datetime
and end_datetime are applied client-side over the most recent messages this tool walks from
upstream: it may miss older matches beyond that window, and the response's scanned_count
field reports how many messages were inspected before filtering.

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: The ID of the channel to get the messages of.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The name of the channel to get the messages of.

parameters.name: channel_id_or_name
parameters.description: The ID or name of the channel to get the messages of. Equivalent to providing either channel_id or channel_name; use whichever of the three parameters is convenient.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Each message can carry a large amount of content (body, mentions, embedded replies), so keep this small unless a wide history scan is actually needed. Defaults to 15, max is 50.

parameters.name: team_id_or_name
parameters.description: The ID or name of the team to get the messages of. If not provided: in case the user is a member of a single team, the tool will use it; otherwise an error will be returned with a list of all teams to pick from.

parameters.name: start_datetime
parameters.description: Only include messages created on or after this moment. Provide a string in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Applied over the most recent messages this tool can fetch in a single call, so an old start_datetime may miss matches if there are more than that many newer messages. Defaults to None (no start date filter).

parameters.name: end_datetime
parameters.description: Only include messages created on or before this moment. Provide a string in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Defaults to None (no end date filter).

tools.name: GetChannelMetadata
tools.description:
Retrieves metadata about a Microsoft Teams channel and its members.

Provide exactly one of channel_id, channel_name, or channel_id_or_name. When available,
prefer providing a channel_id for optimal performance.

The Microsoft Graph API returns only up to the first 999 members in the channel.

This tool does not return messages exchanged in the channel. To retrieve channel messages,
use the `Teams.GetChannelMessages` tool.

It is not necessary to call `Teams.ListTeams` before calling this tool. If the user does not
provide a team_id_or_name, the tool will try to find a unique team to use.

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: The ID of the channel to get. Provide either this or channel_name.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The name of the channel to get. Provide either this or channel_id.

parameters.name: channel_id_or_name
parameters.description: The ID or name of the channel to get. Equivalent to providing either channel_id or channel_name; use whichever of the three parameters is convenient.

parameters.name: team_id_or_name
parameters.description: The ID or name of the team to get the channel of (optional). If not provided: in case the user is a member of a single team, the tool will use it; otherwise an error will be returned with a list of all teams to pick from.

tools.name: GetChatMessages
tools.description:
Retrieves messages from a Microsoft Teams chat (individual or group).

Provide one of chat_id OR any combination of user_ids and/or user_names. When available, prefer
providing a chat_id or user_ids for optimal performance.

If the user provides user name(s), DO NOT CALL THE `Teams.SearchUsers` or `Teams.SearchPeople`
tools first. Instead, provide the user name(s) directly to this tool through the `user_names`
argument. It is not necessary to provide the currently signed in user's name/id, so do not call
`Teams.GetSignedInUser` before calling this tool.

Messages will be sorted in descending order by the messages' `created_datetime` field.

The Microsoft Teams API does not support pagination for this tool.

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: The ID of the chat to get messages from.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The IDs of the users in the chat to get messages from.

parameters.name: user_names
parameters.description: The names of the users in the chat to get messages from. Prefer providing user_ids, when available, since the performance is better.

parameters.name: start_datetime
parameters.description: The start date to filter messages. Provide a string in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Defaults to None (no start date filter).

parameters.name: end_datetime
parameters.description: The end date to filter messages. Provide a string in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Defaults to None (no end date filter).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Each message can carry a large amount of content (body, mentions, attachments), so keep this small unless a wide history scan is actually needed. Defaults to 15, max is 50.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Only include meetings starting on or before this moment. Provide a string in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. tools.name: ReplyToChatMessage
tools.description:
Sends a reply to a Microsoft Teams chat message.

Known limitation: the Microsoft Graph API currently rejects threaded replies in 1:1, group,
and meeting chats with an "unsupported item types" error, regardless of chat, message, or
reply content. This does not affect channel messages; use `Teams.ReplyToChannelMessage` for
those. For 1:1, group, and meeting chats, use `Teams.SendMessageToChat` with its
`quote_message_id` parameter instead, which quotes the target message for reply-with-context
without relying on native threading.

Provide exactly one of chat_id or user_ids/user_names. When available, prefer providing a
chat_id or user_ids for optimal performance.

If the user provides user name(s), DO NOT CALL THE `Teams.SearchUsers` or `Teams.SearchPeople`
tools first. Instead, provide the user name(s) directly to this tool through the `user_names`
argument. It is not necessary to provide the currently signed in user's name/id, so do not call
`Teams.GetSignedInUser` before calling this tool either.

When user_names is provided instead of chat_id, this tool also searches the caller's People
(contacts and interaction history) to resolve the chat.

parameters.name: reply_content

tools.name: SearchPeople
tools.description:
Searches for people the user has interacted with in Microsoft Teams and other 365 products.

This tool only returns users that the currently signed in user has interacted with. It may also
include people that are part of external tenants/organizations. If you need to retrieve users
that may not have interacted with the current user and/or that are exclusively part of the same
tenant, use the `Teams.SearchUsers` tool instead.

Results are ranked by an opaque relevance graph, not a plain name match: a person the caller
has genuinely messaged or chatted with can still be absent from the results for a given
keyword. Do not conclude "no such person" from an empty result; fall back to
`Teams.SearchUsers` or `Teams.SearchTeamMembers` before reporting that no match was found.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: The keywords to match against people's names. Provide one or more expressions.

parameters.name: match_type

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of people to return. Defaults to 50, max is 100.

are from external tenants/organizations, use `Teams.SearchPeople`, instead.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: The keywords to match against users' names.

parameters.name: match_type
parameters.description: The type of match to use for the keywords. Defaults to match_any_of_the_keywords.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of users to return. Defaults to 50, max is 999.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The offset to start from.

When available, prefer providing a channel_id for optimal performance.

It is not necessary to call `Teams.ListTeams` before calling this tool. If the user does not

tools.name: SendMessageToChat
tools.description:
Sends a message to a Microsoft Teams chat.

Provide exactly one of chat_id or user_ids/user_names. When available, prefer providing a
chat_id or user_ids for optimal performance.

Set quote_message_id to reply to an earlier message in the chat: Microsoft Graph does not
support true threaded replies in 1:1, group, or meeting chats (only channel messages support
that; use `Teams.ReplyToChannelMessage` there), so this quotes the target message's sender
and content at the top of the new message instead of threading under it.

If the user provides user name(s), DO NOT CALL THE `Teams.SearchUsers` or `Teams.SearchPeople`
tools first. Instead, provide the user name(s) directly to this tool through the `user_names`
argument. It is not necessary to provide the currently signed in user's name/id, so do not call
`Teams.GetSignedInUser` before calling this tool either.

When user_names is provided instead of chat_id, this tool also searches the caller's People
(contacts and interaction history) to resolve the chat.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The message to send to the chat.

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: The ID of the chat to send the message.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The IDs of the users in the chat to send the message.

parameters.name: user_names
parameters.description: The names of the users in the chat to send the message. Prefer providing user_ids, when available, since the performance is better.

parameters.name: quote_message_id
parameters.description: The ID of an earlier message in this chat to quote at the top of the new message, as a stand-in for a threaded reply. Omit to send a plain message with no quote.

message.value: Hey team, the project review meeting is confirmed for Thursday at 2 PM. Please come prepared with your status updates!

tools.name: UpdateChatMembers
tools.description:
Adds members to, or removes members from, the roster of an existing Microsoft Teams
group chat.

Unlike `Teams.CreateChat`, which creates a brand-new chat (or reuses one only when the
requested member set is an exact match for an existing chat), this tool mutates chat_id's
roster in place, preserving the chat's id and message history for all members.

this way. Provide at least one of user_ids or user_names.

summary:
The Microsoft Teams toolkit connects Arcade to Microsoft Teams via the Microsoft Graph API, enabling LLMs to read and write messages, manage chats and channels, schedule meetings, and look up users across a tenant.

## Capabilities

- **Messaging — chats & channels:** Send, edit, soft-delete, and react to messages in 1:1 chats, group chats, and channel threads; quote messages for reply-with-context in non-channel chats; create and manage group chat rosters.
- **Chat & channel discovery:** List, search, and retrieve metadata (members, settings) for chats, channels, teams, and team members; search messages across the tenant.
- **Meetings:** Schedule, retrieve, list, cancel, and fetch transcripts (with speaker attribution) for Teams online meetings; list generated transcripts per meeting.
- **User & people lookup:** Resolve users by name or ID within the tenant (`SearchUsers`, `ListUsers`), search the signed-in user's interaction graph (`SearchPeople`), and retrieve the caller's own identity and full profile.
- **Team & channel management:** List and search teams and channels; retrieve team metadata; send and reply to channel messages with automatic team resolution when only a name is provided.

## OAuth

This toolkit authenticates via OAuth 2.0 with **Microsoft** as the identity provider. See the [Arcade Microsoft auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/microsoft) for setup details, required app registration steps, and permission configuration.
